findings.title: Salesforce refresh result is discarded and prisma is not imported
findings.body: getClient now does a token refresh and saves the result to the DB, but the Connection is still built from the old credentialKey.access_token and instance_url. The freshly refreshed token is never used, so it can still be expired. The file also calls prisma.credential.update without importing prisma, which fails at compile time or throws a ReferenceError at runtime. The refresh also bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, so the credential sync endpoint is never used for Salesforce. In addition, parseRefreshTokenResponse sets refresh_token to the placeholder string "refresh_token", and the spread of accessTokenParsed.data puts that placeholder into the stored key before it is overridden, which is confusing and fragile.

findings.title: Broken zod schema using computed keys from toString()
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` evaluates to a literal key such as "[object Object]" or "ZodString". It does not create an index signature. The minimum schema therefore requires a bogus key and fails to validate real responses, or it silently strips the expiry field. The second computed key has the same problem. A passthrough schema with a proper check is needed.

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token is written into the response data
findings.body: When the response has no refresh_token, the code sets it to the literal "refresh_token". This fake value can be persisted and later sent to providers as a real refresh token. The mutation also bypasses the schemas, and `.data.refresh_token` does not type-check against the minimal schema.

findings.title: Sync endpoint request is unauthenticated and its errors are unchecked
findings.body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no secret or auth header and does not check response.ok. A failed response is passed on as if it were a token response. The response shape also differs by caller: some callers expect an axios `.data`, while this returns a fetch Response, so callers such as zoho and googlecalendar break in sync mode.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with !==, and request body parsing is unguarded
findings.body: The secret is compared with a plain `!==`, which is not timing-safe. The zod `parse` and `JSON.parse` calls throw uncaught on malformed input, producing a 500 instead of a 400. There is also no method check. The decrypted keys are written to the DB without validation.

findings.title: parseRefreshTokenResponse result stored directly as the credential key
findings.body: `key` is the safeParse result object ({success, data}), not the parsed data. It is written to prisma as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential. Previously `.parse()` returned the data itself.
